title: From the door-counting machinery to Tucker's actual conclusion
content: The header frames the entry against sixteen prior iterations of the sperner-mathlib4-oq-02 program. Those iterations machine-checked every STRUCTURAL piece of the door-counting proof of Tucker's lemma — the abstract path-following and handshaking engines, the fact that the concrete hexagon DOOR GRAPH is a disjoint union of paths and cycles, and the odd oriented BOUNDARY SEED (the hemisphere sign-degree). None of them stated Tucker's actual CONCLUSION: that, for an antipodally-labelled triangulation of B², some edge is complementary (its endpoints carry antipodal labels {k, −k}). This entry supplies that conclusion for the standard hexagon + centre triangulation of B². Honest status: a concrete verification for one coarse triangulation by exhaustive kernel decide over its 256 labellings, 0 sorries and 0 axioms (propext / Quot.sound only, no Lean.ofReduceBool); it is not a dimension-free proof of Tucker.
mathContext: Tucker's lemma: for an antipodally symmetric triangulation of $B^n$ and a labelling $\lambda : V \to \{\pm1,\dots,\pm n\}$ with $\lambda(-v) = -\lambda(v)$ on $\partial B^n = S^{n-1}$, some edge $\{u,w\}$ is complementary: $\lambda(u) = -\lambda(w)$. Here $n = 2$, labels lie in $\{\pm1,\pm2\}$, and the triangulation is the hexagon boundary hexagon coned to its centre.

title: The antipodal labelling model on the hexagon disk
content: Labels {+1,+2,−1,−2} are encoded as Fin 4 with the negation map negL = ![2,3,0,1]; negL_involutive and negL_free record that negL is a fixed-point-free involution, so it genuinely models label antipody. The six boundary vertices are given labels V a b c = ![a, b, c, negL a, negL b, negL c] from three free labels a,b,c on v₀,v₁,v₂ — the antipodal boundary condition v_{i+3} = negL v_i is built in and confirmed by V_antipodal (proved by decide). This is exactly the encoding of the sibling hexagon files SpernerTuckerHexagon and SpernerTuckerHexagonFullDoorGraph, so the model is shared across the n = 2 entries. The seventh vertex — the interior centre — is not part of V; its label is the free variable d supplied to the theorems.
mathContext: Boundary vertices $v_0,\dots,v_5$ of the hexagon $S^1$ with $v_{i+3} = -v_i$; the antipodal action $i \mapsto i+3$ on $\mathrm{Fin}\,6$ is free, so the boundary labelling is a genuine antipodal labelling of $S^1$. The centre vertex has an unconstrained (interior) label $d$.

title: Complementary spokes and boundary edges
content: An edge is complementary when one endpoint's label is the antipode of the other's. The twelve edges of the hexagon + centre triangulation split into six spokes centre–vᵢ (endpoint labels (d, vᵢ)) and six boundary edges vᵢ–v_{i+1}, cyclic in Fin 6 (endpoint labels (vᵢ, v_{i+1})). spokeCompl a b c d := ∃ i : Fin 6, d = negL (V a b c i) says some spoke is complementary; boundaryCompl a b c := ∃ i : Fin 6, V a b c (i+1) = negL (V a b c i) says some boundary edge is complementary. Both are given explicit Decidable instances, so the exhaustive search over all labellings runs inside the kernel via plain decide (no native_decide, hence no Lean.ofReduceBool).
mathContext: Complementary edge $\{u,w\}$: $\lambda(u) = \mathrm{negL}(\lambda(w))$. Spokes contribute $d = \mathrm{negL}(v_i)$; boundary edges contribute $v_{i+1} = \mathrm{negL}(v_i)$ with indices cyclic modulo 6.

title: Tucker's lemma for the hexagon disk, and its 2-dimensionality
content: tucker_hexagon decides spokeCompl a b c d ∨ boundaryCompl a b c over all 4⁴ = 256 antipodal labellings — the conclusion of Tucker's lemma at n = 2: a complementary edge always exists. exists_complementary_edge restates it with the two endpoint labels unpacked. The result is then shown to be genuinely two-dimensional by boundary_ring_insufficient: it decides that some antipodal boundary labelling has NO complementary boundary edge (24 of the 64 boundary labellings), so the already-verified 1-D (S¹) Tucker does not by itself produce the edge — the interior is essential. All #print axioms report propext / Quot.sound only (plain kernel decide, no Lean.ofReduceBool).
mathContext: $\forall\,a,b,c,d,\ (\exists i,\ d = \mathrm{negL}(v_i)) \lor (\exists i,\ v_{i+1} = \mathrm{negL}(v_i))$; yet $\exists a,b,c,\ \neg(\exists i,\ v_{i+1} = \mathrm{negL}(v_i))$ — the boundary ring alone can fail.

title: The interior spoke rescues the boundary (the n = 1 → n = 2 step)
content: interior_spoke_rescues is the constructive heart of the entry: whenever the boundary ring carries no complementary edge (¬ boundaryCompl a b c), some spoke centre–vᵢ is complementary — for EVERY centre label d. The proof reverts all four labels and closes by a single decide over the finite Fin-4 alphabet. Conceptually this is the concrete n = 1 → n = 2 cone step of Tucker's lemma: the boundary is an n = 1 Tucker instance on the antipodal ring, and when it fails, the interior cone over it repairs the failure, guaranteeing a complementary edge regardless of the centre label. Paired with boundary_ring_insufficient, it pinpoints exactly why the hexagon disk is not reducible to its boundary circle. The closing #print axioms confirm all four results rest only on propext / Quot.sound.
mathContext: $\neg(\exists i,\ v_{i+1} = \mathrm{negL}(v_i)) \Rightarrow \forall d,\ \exists i,\ d = \mathrm{negL}(v_i)$: the interior cone repairs the boundary's failure for every centre label.
